questions.question: Which level of biodiversity concerns differences within a species?
choices: Species diversity
Genetic diversity
Ecosystem diversity
Habitat area alone

questions.question: What does species richness measure?
choices: Total individuals present
Number of equally abundant species
Total habitat area
Number of species present

questions.question: What is an endemic species?
choices: A species native to a limited geographic area
Any introduced species
A species found worldwide
Any domesticated species

questions.question: What is habitat fragmentation?
choices: Increasing one continuous habitat's size
Restoring all original vegetation
Breaking habitat into separated patches
Mixing genes within one population

questions.question: What is an invasive species in a conservation context?
choices: Every species moving within its native range
Every newly discovered species
A nonnative species causing ecological or other harm
A native species with many individuals

questions.question: What is an ecosystem service?
choices: A benefit people obtain from ecological processes
A cost of managing protected habitats
A survey of species distributions
A species' role within its own population

questions.question: What is extinction?
choices: Seasonal movement to another region
A decline in one local population only
A temporary change in feeding behavior
Loss of all members of a species

questions.question: Why can genetic diversity matter during environmental change?
choices: Every inherited trait is equally suited to new conditions
Different inherited traits may support different responses
Genetic variation matters only when habitats stay constant
Individual organisms acquire whichever inherited traits they need

questions.question: How can a habitat corridor support conservation?
choices: It can connect populations and allow movement
It makes every habitat patch equally suitable
It prevents movement between connected populations
It replaces the need to protect breeding habitat

questions.question: Why can protecting one habitat help several species?
choices: Protecting a habitat removes its species' different needs
Each species uses resources independently of other species
Species share resources and ecological relationships
Only the most abundant species benefits from protection

questions.question: Why can a nonnative species become harmful in a new ecosystem?
choices: Introduced species always encounter the same controls as at home
Local controls may be absent and interactions may change
Nonnative status alone guarantees severe ecological harm
Native populations cannot be affected by new competitors

questions.question: How does overharvesting threaten populations?
choices: Harvested populations necessarily replace all removed individuals
Harvesting affects individual organisms but not population growth
Only habitat loss can cause long-term population decline
Removal can exceed reproduction and replenishment

questions.question: Why can conservation planning use both richness and abundance data?
choices: Species richness measures the population size of each species
Abundance data show habitat quality without species information
Equal richness means two communities have equal evenness
Species counts alone omit population sizes and evenness

questions.question: Why might a small isolated population face genetic risks?
choices: Isolation creates unlimited new alleles
Limited gene flow and chance allele loss can reduce variation
Small populations never experience drift
All recessive alleles disappear automatically

questions.question: Why should restoration success be monitored over time?
choices: The first year's results establish permanent recovery
Recovery is measured only by the number of seedlings planted
Recovery can vary and require revised management
Management choices cannot influence later outcomes

questions.question: Two habitats each contain ten species, but one is dominated by one species. Which measure differs most directly?
choices: Species evenness
Species richness
Number of named species
The definition of species

questions.question: A road separates breeding populations. Which action may directly restore movement if suitable for the species?
choices: Fencing the entire road without passages
A properly designed wildlife crossing
Widening the road across the same habitat
Planting food sources only beside traffic lanes

questions.question: Pollinator numbers decline while dependent plants set fewer seeds. What relationship should be investigated?
choices: Pollination supporting plant reproduction
A shift in plants' preferred soil minerals
Plant reproduction requiring no pollen transfer
Seed consumers increasing pollinator reproduction

questions.question: Harvest removes 120 individuals yearly while replacement adds 80, with other changes absent. What is expected?
choices: An increase of 40 yearly
No change
A decline of 40 individuals yearly
An increase of 200 yearly

questions.question: A conservation proposal protects varied habitat types rather than one uniform patch. Which benefit is plausible?
choices: Ensuring the same species occupy every habitat
Favoring only species that need uniform conditions
Making habitat management unnecessary
Supporting species with different habitat requirements
